details.readme:
The open-source AI video editor: create, edit, remake.

Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Download the app · Quickstart · Showcase · Catalog · Docs · Discord · X · YouTube

HyperFrames is HeyGen's AI video editor for people and agents. Describe a video, bring your own footage, or remake a video you love, and get a real project you can change down to the frame: ask for a bigger title, a faster cut or new captions, and it changes just that. Underneath, HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework (Apache 2.0) for turning HTML, CSS, JavaScript, media and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex and Cursor with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. No React required. ## Three ways to use it | | Best for | Start | | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **HyperFrames Studio app** | Anyone, no code. Describe a video or drop in your footage, then edit by typing or pointing. Use the built-in agent on Pro, or your own Claude Code or Codex. | [Download for Mac, Windows or Linux](https://hyperframes.studio/studio/download?src=github-readme) (free plan) | | **Your coding agent** | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other agents. | `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes` | | **Claude, ChatGPT or Grok** (beta) | Making a video in a chat, nothing to install. ChatGPT: Business, Enterprise and Edu workspaces. | Connect [HyperFrames by HeyGen](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/mcp?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme), listed in [Claude's connector directory](https://claude.com/connectors/hyperframes-heygen) | The [HyperFrames Studio app](https://hyperframes.studio/studio?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme) has a free plan. [Pro](https://hyperframes.studio/pricing?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme) ($25 a month) adds top video, image, voice and music models (HeyGen Video 1, Seedance 2.5, Lyria 3 Pro and more) and 25,000 credits a month. ## Made with HyperFrames

repository.description: The AI-native engine for teams and their agents. Multi-harness, multi-agent, self-hosted.

details.readme:
**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) > **中文文档入口：[文档目录](docs/README.zh-CN.md) · [安装与启动](docs/getting-started.md) · [开发指南](docs/development.md)**
# SoduWork ## The AI-native engine for teams and their agents **A chat ends with an answer. A SoduWork request ends when the person who asked signs off.** **Multi-harness · Multi-agent · Self-hosted** Works with Pi · OpenCode · DeepSeek Harness · Qwen Code · Kimi Code · Codex Harness · Codex **Run from source** ```sh git clone https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork cd SoduWork ``` | Platform | Start command | | --- | --- | | macOS / Linux | `sh start.sh --desktop` | | Windows PowerShell | `.\start.cmd --desktop` | | Windows Command Prompt | `start.cmd --desktop` | For source setup, we recommend [Python 3.12.x](https://www.python.org/downloads/) and [Node.js 22.x](https://nodejs.org/) (22.19.0 or later in that series). The clone command uses [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads). **[Windows desktop app](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases/latest)** | [Website](https://soduwork.ai) | [Live demo](https://soduwork.ai) | [Documentation](docs/README.md) | [Docs website](https://dev.soduwork.ai) | [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases) | [Discord](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/mdiri-ai/SoduWork)](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases) [![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)](#quick-start) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-Discord-5865F2.svg)](https://discord.gg/AXYNrAYHy)
--- ## What SoduWork can do for you | | | | --- | --- | | **One harness does the work, another reviews it** | Pick Pi to do the work. OpenCode, on a different model, reviews it against the acceptance criteria. If the review fails, the work goes back with the reasons. | | **Hand a request to a colleague's agent** | People and AI work together: you file a request, AI writes the acceptance criteria, and you assign it to yourself or a colleague. The assignee's agent does the work and reviews it, and a person signs off. Everyone on the request can see who did what. | | **Turn one person's know-how into a team asset** | When you and AI get a task right, save the chat as a plugin. After review, anyone on the team can use it and contribute improvements, with access granted as needed. | ## Core ideas
**🔀 Smart dispatch** **The right agent and model for each job.** - Pick a harness for each step and switch mid-conversation - Routine steps on cheap or local models, strong models where it matters - Long tasks go to your own cloud runner **🛡️ Built-in governance** **Your organization decides which AI does what, and where.** - Plugins are reviewed before they are shared, granted to teams or people, and can be revoked - Roles, usage, cost and an audit log - Self-hosted **✅ Verified delivery** **Set the bar first. Done means the requester signed off.** - Every request carries its acceptance criteria - A separate AI review checks each one - A person makes the final call
## Quick start > SoduWork is in public beta. Try it and tell us what you think, and evaluate it before using it in production. Clone the repository with Git or extract a source archive. See the [source setup guide](docs/getting-started.en.md) for prerequisites. From the repository root, run `sh start.sh --desktop` on macOS/Linux, `.\start.cmd --desktop` in Windows PowerShell, or `start.cmd --desktop` in Command Prompt. If Windows says a command “is not recognized”, check which command it names. For `git`, `python` or `node`, check that the corresponding tool is installed and on `PATH`, then reopen Command Prompt. See the [source setup guide](docs/getting-started.en.md). The first run installs dependencies, then starts the Hub, the admin console and the desktop client on this computer. Set a password for the `admin` account (12–128 characters) when asked. Then add a model provider under **Model catalog** in the admin console, start a chat in the client and try a small task. Pi is built in. ### Already added an API key? Start here 1. **Add a chat model as well.** Under **Capabilities → Model catalog**, find the service you connected, choose **Add model**, enter the provider's exact model ID, select **Chat model**, and save. Saving a service credential alone does not create a selectable model. 2. **Open the desktop client and sign in to the same Hub.** Use `--desktop` when starting from source. The browser admin console configures the service; check that **Connection** on the desktop sign-in screen points to that same Hub. 3. **Choose New conversation, Pi, and the model you added.** Pi uses the SoduWork model catalog. Codex uses its own account and needs its own sign-in; it does not automatically use this API key. 4. **Try a small task.** For example: “Turn these fictional meeting notes into an action table with owner and due date. Mark missing information as unconfirmed: Alex will organize the requirements by Friday; Sam will check the quotation.” Check the returned table against the notes. 5. **Create a requirement when you need assignment and acceptance.** Describe the goal, inputs and acceptance criteria, open **Arrange execution**, choose an Agent and model, and inspect the delivery before accepting it. A normal conversation does not require a project, plugin or automation first. For the first message, use an **OpenAI-compatible chat model with Pi**. A successful connection probe does not guarantee a successful inference: balance, model permissions and protocol support still matter. If the Agent list is empty, check **Agent management** and the Runner connection. If the model list is empty, check that the model exists, is enabled, and both interfaces use the same Hub. See [Run from source: send your first AI message](docs/getting-started.en.md#send-your-first-ai-message) for field-by-field setup and troubleshooting.
Try the live demo Download the client from [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases/latest), enter `https://service.soduwork.ai` under **Connection** on the sign-in screen, then sign up and sign in. > The demo is for evaluation only. Don't upload real business data or anything sensitive.
Install the desktop client Follow the illustrated [desktop installation and first conversation guide](docs/desktop-quickstart.en.md). | OS | Package | | --- | --- | | Windows | `SoduWork--Setup.exe` | | macOS (Apple Silicon / Intel) | `SoduWork--mac-.dmg` | | Linux | `SoduWork--linux.deb` / `.rpm` / `.tar.gz` | Download from [Releases](https://github.com/mdiri-ai/SoduWork/releases). On first launch, enter your Hub address under **Connection**, then sign in. On macOS, if you see "cannot verify the developer", open **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and choose **Open Anyway**.
Deploy for a team with Docker With Docker installed and running, from the repository root: ```bash python3 ops/self-host/deploy.py up python3 ops/self-host/deploy.py credentials # show the initial admin password ``` This starts the Hub, the admin console and PostgreSQL on one server. Put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of it to open it to your team. See [Deploy with Docker](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/docker) and [Deploy for a team](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/deploy).
Ports, data folders and troubleshooting are in [Run from source](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/run-from-source) and the [FAQ](https://dev.soduwork.ai/docs/get-started/faq). ## Why SoduWork AI agents give everyone fast output. What no one gets for free is trust in that output — or a way to keep what worked. That's where individuals and teams get stuck alike: | The problem | What SoduWork does | | --- | --- | | **Fast output, slow trust** — whether you work alone or in a team, the time AI saves goes back into checking what it produced | **The request is the spec.** Criteria set before work starts; a separate AI review checks each one; a person signs off | | **What worked dies in a chat thread** — for one person, it's last month's perfect run you can't reproduce; for a team, it's one person's method nobody else can use | **Get it right once, keep it as a plugin.** Reuse it yourself or publish it for everyone — every improvement reaches everyone | | **A drawer full of AI tools** — three subscriptions and no standard for which one does what | **One workbench, your playbook.** Your plugins run on every harness. Switch mid-conversation, keep your history and files | | **Results that never enter the workflow** — output gets copy-pasted around, and every handoff re-explains the background | **Issues that carry the context.** People and agents pick up where it left off, with a full record of who did what | ## How it works Requests, execution, review and reuse all happen in one shared issue pool: ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Raise a request] --> B[AI refines it
adds acceptance criteria] B --> C[Assign
yourself · a colleague · an agent] C --> D[Agent runs it
with a team plugin] D --> E[AI review
assignee confirms] E --> F[Requester signs off] F --> G[Save as a plugin] G -.reused by the team.-> D ``` | Role | Where they join | | --- | --- | | **Solo developer** | Puts requests in the pool, lets agents work through them, and only signs off | | **Specialist** | Gets a task right with AI, saves the method as a plugin, and publishes it to the team | | **Manager** | Drops in a request; AI fills in the criteria and routes it to a person or an agent; signs off at the end | | **New team member** | Uses the plugins the organization has built up to do the work to team standards, and improves them when they find a gap | Who asked, who did the work, which plugin ran and who approved it is always on record. ## Multi-harness · Multi-agent A harness is the agent runtime that does the work. It is not the model. SoduWork connects every harness through one adapter interface, so issues, plugins and review don't depend on any single harness. Switch harnesses mid-conversation and keep the history and the working folder. Programs that support the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) can be added with a catalog declaration.
Supported harnesses (7) | Harness | Models | How it connects | | --- | --- | --- | | Pi | Your SoduWork models | Built in | | OpenCode | Your SoduWork models | Native adapter, installed on demand | | DeepSeek Harness | Your SoduWork models, or your own DeepSeek key | ACP, installed on demand | | Qwen Code | Your SoduWork models | ACP, installed on demand | | Kimi Code | Your SoduWork models | ACP, installed on demand | | Codex Harness | Your SoduWork models | ACP, installed on demand | | Codex | Its own OpenAI account | Native adapter, installed on demand |
Agents work together at several levels: | Level | Who decides | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | Harness | The harness itself | OpenCode or Qwen Code starts its own subagents to explore the code or split

details.readme:
The open-source Claude Motion & CapCut alternative

Install · Agents · Use cases & remakes · Why OpenMotion · Setup & architecture · Community

**English** · [简体中文](docs/README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](docs/README.ja.md)
# OpenMotion OpenMotion is a **full-stack agentic video** studio and an **open-source alternative to Claude Motion and CapCut**. Upload a reference video or paste a social video link to **recreate it with your own brand kit and copy**. - 🎬 **Full-stack video recreation.** Code video with HTML. Your agent breaks down the reference, rebuilds its shots and transitions, and generates missing assets. Edit the timing in Studio and render an MP4 from the same project. - 🔑 **BYOA — Bring Your Own Agent. BYOK — Bring Your Own Keys.** OpenMotion is free and open source. Recreate videos in [your local agent](#agent-wall) with your own API keys. Supported agents include Claude Code, Codex, and WorkBuddy. - 🧩 OpenMotion introduces **Motion.md**, a Markdown format for shot order, timing and transitions. Use it to share how a brand film works, shot by shot. - 🎛️ **Images, video, music and voice.** Create artwork with GPT Image 2.6, add a shot with Seedance 2.5, score it with Suno and narrate it with Eleven v4. [Explore the models and providers](#model-wall). ### Install from ChatGPT Marketplace **One-click installation. No manual configuration required.** Once installed, create motion videos from scratch, recreate reference videos, or start from a template—all in your conversation. **[Install OpenMotion in ChatGPT →](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6a742d13e88481919b42002864b1bb26)** ### Install in your agent Install the main Skill with the [Skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills): ```sh npx skills add nexu-io/openmotion --skill openmotion ``` Then ask your agent: **Use OpenMotion to connect Cloud MCP, then help me make a video.** The Skill connects directly to the hosted Streamable HTTP `/mcp` endpoint via OAuth 2.1 without installing a local runtime, and reuses an existing working connection. Installing the Skill alone copies instructions; it does not yet connect MCP. Copy this instruction into your agent to connect OpenMotion Cloud MCP: ```text Read https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion/blob/main/docs/install.md and follow the instructions to connect OpenMotion in the current agent. ``` After OAuth authorization, the agent opens the cloud template library and shows the localized welcome followed by three curated project-preview cards via a native MCP App, self-contained HTML document, DSH card, or text fallback. Each onboarding samples three distinct entries from the curated pool of four without waiting for native MCP tool reload or fetching remote reference films for inline previews. Preview a card, choose **Recreate template**, then send your brief to start creating. [Cloud MCP connection guide](docs/install.md) · [Onboarding reply rules](docs/install.md#installation-success-reply) ### Legacy local source & npm installation (optional) Cloud MCP setup above is the default Agent connection path. For self-hosted deployments see [deploy/README.md](deploy/README.md). Legacy local source/stdio setup and published npm application recipes remain archived for explicit local use: ```text Read https://releases.open-design.ai/motion and follow the instructions to install and connect the published npm application in the current agent. ``` [Archived legacy local source & npm guide](docs/templates/legacy-npm-install.md) · [npm installation and diagnostics](docs/npm-installation.md). Published npm versions can lag behind this checkout. ### Run the repository locally Use Git, npm and Node.js 26.11.1: ```sh git -c filter.lfs.process= -c filter.lfs.smudge= -c filter.lfs.required=false clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch main https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion.git cd openmotion npm ci npm run build:studio npm start ``` Open the actual `studioUrl` or `previewUrl` printed at startup, then choose **Template library**. Studio and MCP read the templates in this checkout. To connect your agent to this same copy, follow [source setup and MCP configuration](#agent-setup). [Clone size and optional media](docs/repository-storage.md) ### Start from an existing project Import a **HyperFrames project ZIP** into OpenMotion to continue editing its composition and local assets. Compress the project folder, open **All projects → Import projects**, then select the imported copy to edit in Studio or with your Agent. Import creates an independent copy and requires a supported native project structure. [Step-by-step import guide, required files and compatibility](docs/project-archives.md#import-from-hyperframes) **22 local agents** · [Choose your agent](#choose-agent)

## 🎞️ Use cases and remake examples Explore product demos, brand films, talking-head videos and more. The previews below show reference videos. **[Browse the full template library →](https://open-design.ai/templates/)** — Find more templates, full videos, Motion.md and recreation instructions. ### AI recuts & revisions

OpenAI · Build a story from multiple scenes
Connect different scenes around one narrative idea, then expand into a broader montage.
View template

repository.description: Observability and enforcement for AI agent harnesses. Capture every run and runtime reliability with policy enforcement.

details.readme:
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/failproofai?style=flat-square&color=CB3837)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/failproofai) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/failproofai/failproofai/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=CI)](https://github.com/failproofai/failproofai/actions) [![Supply Chain](https://img.shields.io/badge/supply%20chain-secure-brightgreen?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/failproofai/failproofai/actions/workflows/osv-scanner.yml) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join%20us-5865F2?style=flat-square&logo=discord)](https://discord.befailproof.ai/) [![Reddit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Reddit-r%2Ffailproofai-FF4500?style=flat-square&logo=reddit)](https://www.reddit.com/r/failproofai/) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-befailproof.ai-002CA7?style=flat-square)](https://docs.befailproof.ai/) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20%2B%20Commons%20Clause-blue?style=flat-square)](./LICENSE) **Translations:** [简体中文](./docs/i18n/README.zh.md) · [日本語](./docs/i18n/README.ja.md) · [한국어](./docs/i18n/README.ko.md) · [Español](./docs/i18n/README.es.md) · [Português](./docs/i18n/README.pt-br.md) · [Deutsch](./docs/i18n/README.de.md) · [Français](./docs/i18n/README.fr.md) · [Русский](./docs/i18n/README.ru.md) · [हिन्दी](./docs/i18n/README.hi.md) · [Türkçe](./docs/i18n/README.tr.md) · [Tiếng Việt](./docs/i18n/README.vi.md) · [Italiano](./docs/i18n/README.it.md) · [العربية](./docs/i18n/README.ar.md) · [עברית](./docs/i18n/README.he.md) ## Ship agents that never fail. Your agent ran `rm -rf` on the wrong directory. It read `.env` into its context. It spent forty minutes retrying the same broken call, then told you the task was done. **Failproof lives in your agent's runtime and hears every hook event it fires**: the session starting, every prompt, every tool call and its result, sub-agents spinning up, context about to be compacted, the moment it tries to stop. **It can act on any of them**: block the bad action before it executes, steer the agent mid-run, or send it back to work when it quits too early. Then it learns from every failure, so your agent's harness gets better with every run. **37% → 69%** task success on failures a policy recognised. Same model, no fine-tuning ([FIRE study](https://befailproof.ai/research/runtime-policies/))
**~0.7 ms** p50 per policy check, from a Rust daemon in the hot path
**12 agent harnesses**, one policy API: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes, OpenClaw and more Open source and free to start. Install the CLI, connect Failproof Cloud, and your first audit runs on your agents' real history.

--- ## Supported harnesses Twelve harnesses in two classes: ten coding CLIs, and two chat and assistant gateways (Hermes, OpenClaw). Building your own agent, on any framework or none? Report its runs through the [Python SDK](https://docs.befailproof.ai/reference/custom-agents) or the [TypeScript SDK](https://docs.befailproof.ai/reference/custom-agents-typescript), which give you tracing, sessions, evaluations and audits. Enforcement there needs a hook in your own runtime. [Talk to us](mailto:support@befailproof.ai) and we'll map it.
--- ## Get started: find where your agents fail, then stop it ```sh npm install -g failproofai failproofai config # hook your agents, connect to Failproof Cloud (free) failproofai backfill --since 7d # bring in the last week of runs already on disk ``` 1. **Connect.** `failproofai config` finds every agent on this machine, hooks into each one, starts the background daemon, and signs you in to Failproof Cloud in your browser. No account yet? Make one right there, on the free plan. 2. **Backfill.** Your agents have been running for weeks, and that history is already on this machine. `failproofai backfill --since 7d` sends the last seven days ([for supported harnesses](https://docs.befailproof.ai/reference/failproof-cli#backfill-per-harness)), so you start with real evidence instead of an empty dashboard. 3. **Audit.** The moment runs land, Cloud starts your first audit on its own. It reads your sessions, clusters what went wrong into named failure modes, and turns each one into an **insight**, with the sessions that prove it. The free plan includes audits every month. 4. **Plug in policies built for your agents.** Open an insight and hit **prevent this →**. Failproof drafts a policy for that exact failure and tests it against your agents' own past tool calls. You then roll it out to every machine, watching first or enforcing straight away. Setting up CI, a container, or letting an agent run the install? `failproofai config` notices there's no one to ask and applies the defaults without prompting. --- ## One policy, every harness Every harness speaks its own dialect: - Claude Code reads a JSON verdict, while Factory's droid only stops on exit code 2. - Cursor forces another turn with a `followup_message`. - OpenCode and OpenClaw have no shell hooks at all, only in-process plugins, and Hermes loads a native Python plugin. - Even the shell tool has six names: `Bash`, `terminal`, `Execute`, `shell`, `run_command`, `exec`. Failproof translates all of it: - Every event maps onto one canonical set of 29 (`SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `Stop`, …). - Every tool name and argument maps onto one canonical form. - Every verdict is translated back into the exact shape that harness obeys. So a policy written once against `Bash` blocks the same command in Claude Code, Codex, Hermes and Goose. A "run the tests before you stop" gate sends the agent back to work on every harness that has a turn-end hook. Each contract is verified against that CLI and pinned, with what it was verified on, in a capability matrix the test suite checks every claim against. Blocking before a tool runs is verified on all twelve harnesses; turn-end gates on eight. The [per-harness matrix](https://docs.befailproof.ai/reference/harnesses#enforcement-capability) shows exactly which events each one honours. --- ## Policies, written for your agents A policy can listen to any of those events. Before a tool call, it can block the command outright. When a prompt arrives, it can add context. When the agent tries to stop, it can send it back to finish the job. Whatever it decides, the agent is told why. There are two kinds of policy, and you can mix them: - **Code.** Plain JavaScript, for anything you can check exactly: paths, commands, arguments, limits. It's just code, so it can call your own model too. - **Decision model.** Plain-English yes/no questions that Jev, our fast classifier, answers about each call against what the user actually asked for. The `rm -rf build/` you asked for goes through; the `rm -rf ~` that slipped into a plan doesn't. Use it for the judgment calls no regex can make. **You don't have to write either.** Failproof authors them for you. Open an insight

details.readme:
# OpenVideoHarness ### You direct. AI makes the film. An open-source, controllable workflow for making videos with code. Say what you want in one sentence, and a coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex writes the code and renders the film. Every step shows up in Studio: point at a shot, say what to change, and compare the two cuts. Plenty of tools can turn a sentence or two into a video. The hard part is doing it under control, repeatably and at volume, inside your own workflow. That is what this project is for. **[Quick start](#quick-start)** · [5-minute walk-through](https://zlhad.top/OpenVideoHarness/docs/site/?lang=en#tour) · [Studio demo, 17 s with sound](https://zlhad.top/OpenVideoHarness/docs/site/?lang=en#studio) · [Showcase films](#the-5-showcase-films-with-sound) **English** · [中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Website](https://zlhad.top/OpenVideoHarness/docs/site/?lang=en) · [Wiki](https://github.com/ZLHad/OpenVideoHarness/wiki) ![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-black) ![Agents](https://img.shields.io/badge/agents-Claude%20Code%20%7C%20Codex%20%7C%20DeepSeek%20Harness-orange) ![Engines](https://img.shields.io/badge/engines-HyperFrames%20%7C%20canvas%20%2B%20Three.js%20%7C%20p5.brush%20%7C%20Manim%20%7C%20Blender-blue) A 5-minute 17-second walk-through, narrated and subtitled in Chinese: installing it, three ways in, how a real 33-minute film was made step by step, and how it was reviewed in Studio. Click the poster to watch it on the website with sound, or download it in 1080p (164 MB) or 4K (740 MB). It was made with the harness too. All made with it. A dozen films in a month, about 100 minutes in all; the longest runs 33 minutes in 4K. **12 video types · 43 styles · 5 engines · voice, music, sound effects and captions included · runs on your own computer · MIT**
## Quick start You need macOS or Linux, Git, Node.js 22+, Chrome, FFmpeg, Python 3 with [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv), and a signed-in Claude Code or Codex installation. [Requirements and limits](#requirements-cost-and-limits) ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZLHad/OpenVideoHarness/main/install.sh | bash ``` Choose where to start your film. Use whichever suits you: a film started anywhere shows up in Studio. - **Studio.** Open **OVH Studio** from Applications, or run `bin/vh studio` from the install folder. Select Claude Code or Codex in the agent column and choose **Set it up** if the adapter is missing. Send your request there. - **Terminal.** In the default install folder, run `cd ~/OpenVideoHarness && codex` or `cd ~/OpenVideoHarness && claude`, then send your request. - **The Claude Code or Codex desktop app.** Open the install folder (`~/OpenVideoHarness` by default) as the project and send your request. - **From any other folder.** The installer registers a skill named `open-video-harness` with Claude Code and with Codex. So whichever project is open, ask for a video and the agent finds the workbench and follows it. Films go under the workbench's `projects/` unless you name another place. To install the skill alone, see [install options](#install-options-and-updates). For a first run, try this silent sample. > Quick draft: make a silent 15-second vertical explainer showing why doubling a square’s side length quadruples its area. Use a grid and on-screen text. The agent keeps the source and exports together in the film's project folder. With `quick` it goes straight through to a checked video. Ask for `standard` or `studio` to review the direction and draft, with a separate storyboard review when the next step is costly. [Step-by-step guide](https://github.com/ZLHad/OpenVideoHarness/wiki/Getting-Started) · [Install options and updates](#install-options-and-updates)

Making a film in Studio. Along the top, where the film has got to. Point at a few seconds of the timeline, or at a shot, and write a note. On the right, what waits for your decision; send it all together. The film on screen is this repo's own intro film.

## What makes it different

Time is the only input. This flash is counted in microseconds.		 The film is code, so it stays under control.
Every frame depends on time alone, so the same moment always draws the same frame: it can be redone and spot-checked. A few seconds of a finished 4K film can be redrawn and put back without touching the rest. A render that stops picks up where it stopped. Every render is kept as a version, so the cut before and the cut after can be watched side by side.

Studio in 17 seconds: look, point, say, decide. Click for the version with sound.		 The whole process, in one window.
On top of the skills and the command line, we built Studio, a visual window that makes the whole production easier to keep in hand: where each film has got to and who it waits for, at a glance; in review, point at a second and write a line, then hand a few of them to the agent together; what you decide is a few cards, a click each. It comes down to four moves: look at where the film has got to, point at a second or a shot, say what to change, and decide on a card. Its look, its language, the default agent and the API keys of online services are all set on Studio's settings page, with no config file to touch.

Said at the concept stop: "glass, cosmos, a starry sky… dizzying".		 You direct. It does the work.
It stops for you at the concept and the first draft; when the film is long, heavy to render or costs money, at the storyboard too. Want to decide the hook, the voice or the cover as well? Name them. Want none of it? Say "just make it".

A stock chart that is also a mountain range.		 It settles what to say before it starts making.
Two or three concept cards come first, each with a frame and a hook. It says what every other film on your topic looks like, then goes somewhere else.

The agent going through its own frames.		 It checks its own work before you see it.
An agent can't see video or hear sound, so it measures everything it can. It reads contact sheets against a 20-point checklist, measures the sound, and hands the draft to a reviewer with a fresh context, who scores it on 8 points. bin/vh check catches frozen frames, flashes, subtitles too short to read and wrong colour tags, and names a way out of each.

A generated plate, with code on top, both on record.		 Any material can go into the cut.
Pictures drawn in code, archive footage, generated images, 3D models, recorded sound, and your own photos and recordings (those two still experimental) can share one film. One ledger keeps where each file came from, its licence and what it cost. No budget, no paid call.

▶ Press play and turn the sound on: each harmonic sounds its own note.		 Sound is part of the same process.
Voice, music, sound effects and captions are part of the process, so there is nothing to stitch on afterwards. The narration or the music goes down first, every word and beat gets a time, and the picture hangs on those times. The score can be written as code or be a track of your own, and sound effects land on the frame where things happen.

From a film of 33 minutes.		 Long films hold up.
Shots, captions and chapters hang on the narration's words, so adding a pause moves the picture with it. Edit lists join pages and footage, renders resume, and the upload copy fits the platform's limit. The longest so far runs 33 minutes in 4K.
**And it fits into your own workflow.** The whole thing is docs written for an agent plus one command line, `bin/vh`. A film is a folder, and its source, storyboard and review record are text. Switch agents, script it, make a dozen films a month: it is the same process. **Nor is it one AI look.** Left alone, AI video drifts toward one face: dark background, glow, glass cards. Here are 32 of its 43 styles, all rendering the same sentence: ## Studio On top of the skills and the command line, we built Studio, a visual window that makes it easier to keep the whole making of a film in hand. Using it comes down to four things: see where a film has got to, point at the picture and say something, decide on cards, and talk to the agent.

details.readme:
Nomi — open-source, local-first AI video studio

Tell its agent what you want to make. It plans the shots, generates keyframes and video, and lays them on your timeline —
with the models you connect, at the price your provider charges.

Download · Website · AtomGit mirror · Watch the 90-second film · Quick start · Let your AI connect it · Community · 简体中文 · 日本語

## At a glance - **What it is:** a desktop AI video studio. Its agent splits your story into shots, generates keyframes and video, and lays them on a real timeline you can edit and export as MP4. - **Platforms:** macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Windows. - **Price:** Nomi itself is free. You connect your own models and pay the provider directly at their price; no Nomi account, subscription or markup. - **Models:** Seedance, Kling, Wan, Hailuo, Nano Banana, GPT Image and more, through APIMart, Kie.ai, Volcengine, ModelScope, a Dreamina membership, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or your local ComfyUI. - **Agents:** a built-in MCP server lets Claude Code, Codex or Cursor drive Nomi. - **Local-first:** projects, prompts and keys stay on your machine. - **License:** AGPL-3.0-only since 2026-08-01. Releases up to v0.18.1 were published under Apache-2.0 and keep that license. - **Latest version:** see [Releases](https://github.com/aqm857886159/Nomi/releases/latest). - **Name:** this Nomi is an AI video app. It is unrelated to the Nomi AI companion chatbot at nomi.ai. ## Sponsors Sponsors help keep Nomi free and open source. A sponsor never becomes a default or a built-in route: you connect only what you choose, with your own key, and pay them directly at their price. [Want to appear here?](#community)
Gway — an API platform focused on AI video and multi-image reference generation: Seedance 2.0 / 2.5, Wan 3, MiniMax and other mainstream models, OpenAI-compatible, pay-as-you-go. Nomi has no built-in preset for it yet; click Let AI connect it for me and Claude Code or Codex wires it in with your key. Thanks to Gway for sponsoring Nomi! (The Gway links carry a referral code.)
## Why Nomi Relays, official APIs, ComfyUI, and local models are cheap. Commercial AI video products often run the very same models and charge several times more. Nomi gives you a pro-grade workflow on top of **your own** models. You pay your provider directly, at their price. Even the agent runs on the model you pick — no subscription, no markup. ## Watch the film [![Watch the 90-second Nomi 0.22 film](marketing/assets/promo-0.22/film-poster-en.jpg)](https://github.com/aqm857886159/Nomi/blob/main/marketing/assets/video/nomi-0.22-film.mp4) Every screen in the film is Nomi's real UI, and every image and clip in it was generated with Nomi. ## What you can do ### Just ask — the agent works on your canvas Describe the film you want. The agent reads your canvas, splits the story into shots, generates keyframes, turns them into video, and arranges the timeline. Everything it makes lands on the canvas, where you can see it and change it. You decide how much it asks: **Ask each step**, **Auto-edit** (paid generation still asks), or **Full auto**. ### Direct every shot The storyboard puts each shot on one row — prompt, first frame, model, duration. Lock a reference card for a character or a place, and every shot that uses it keeps the same face. ### A 3D director you can hold in your hand Pose characters, place cameras, and use your phone as the viewfinder. The frames you capture go straight back onto the canvas. ### Any model, per shot Seedance, Kling, Wan, Hailuo, Nano Banana, GPT Image and more — through APIMart, Kie.ai, Volcengine, ModelScope, a Dreamina membership, any OpenAI-compatible relay, or your local ComfyUI. Swap the model on a single shot and generate another take. ### New model today, in Nomi today When a new model ships, click **Let AI connect it for me** and let Claude Code or Codex wire it in. It looks up the endpoint, parameters and model IDs, has you paste your key on Nomi's own page (the assistant never sees it), runs one real test, and lists the model once it works. ### Yours A project is a plain folder on your disk: canvas, storyboard, timeline, every generated file, and the exported film. No account. Nothing is sent by default; anonymous usage statistics are opt-in (Settings → Privacy & diagnostics) and can be turned off any time. The code is AGPL-3.0. **Next up: AI editing.** Nomi is heading toward one studio for everything you make with AI — come build it with us. ## Download | System | Build | Download | |---|---|---| | macOS | Apple Silicon | [Nomi-mac-arm64.dmg](https://github.com/aqm857886159/Nomi/releases/latest/download/Nomi-mac-arm64.dmg) | | macOS | Intel | [Nomi-mac-intel.dmg](https://github.com/aqm857886159/Nomi/releases/latest/download/Nomi-mac-intel.dmg) | | Windows | Windows 10 / 11 x64 | [Nomi-windows-setup.exe](https://github.com/aqm857886159/Nomi/releases/latest/download/Nomi-windows-setup.exe) | Supported release targets are macOS arm64/x64 and Windows x64. Linux, Windows arm64, and macOS universal installers are not currently published.
First launch on macOS The current macOS build is **not Apple Developer ID signed or notarized**, so macOS may block it on first launch. Only use the direct downloads above or links from the official Nomi website and GitHub repository. 1. Download the matching DMG, open it, and drag **Nomi** onto **Applications** in the window. 2. Open Nomi from Applications. If macOS says **“Nomi” Not Opened**, click **Done**, then open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down to **Security**, click **Open Anyway** next to the Nomi message, and confirm. Since macOS 15, right-clicking the app and choosing **Open** no longer gets past this prompt; on macOS 14 and earlier it still works. Only if macOS says Nomi is “damaged”, first confirm the installer came from an official Nomi link, then run: ```bash xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Nomi.app" ``` Do not disable Gatekeeper globally. To update, download the matching DMG, quit Nomi, then drag the new Nomi onto Applications and choose **Replace**.
First launch on Windows The installer has no Authenticode signature. In the SmartScreen prompt, choose **More info** → **Run anyway**.
## Quick start 1. **Connect a model.** Pick APIMart or Kie.ai and paste one key — or add your own relay, OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or local ComfyUI. Rather not do it yourself? Hand [Let your AI connect Nomi](docs/integrate-with-your-agent-en.md) to Claude Code or Codex. 2. **Say what you want to make.** Type it into the agent panel, or start from a story in the storyboard. 3. **Direct and export.** Keep the takes you like, arrange the timeline, export MP4. > **Disclosure:** the APIMart link carries a referral code. You always pay providers directly with your own key at their price. Nomi never proxies or resells inference, and every provider can be swapped for your own endpoint. More: [quick start](https://nomiaqm.com/en/quickstart) · [connect your first model (English)](docs/guide/model-connection-en.md) · [user guide](docs/user-guide.md) · [providers](docs/provider-integration.md) · [CLI + MCP](docs/guide/capability-core-cli-mcp.md) ## Use Nomi from your own agent Nomi ships an MCP server with 24 MCP tools, so Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor can drive it — generate, arrange, and edit — while reusing the credits that come with your agent subscription. See [Let your AI connect Nomi](docs/integrate-with-your-agent-en.md). ## Community - Questions, workflows, what's next: [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/aqm857886159/Nomi/discussions) - Bugs and feature requests: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/aqm857886159/Nomi/issues) - Release notes and short demos: [X / Twitter](https://x.com/sdf297417627618) · [Bilibili](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1Lf8b6nEjf/) WeChat users can scan to join the user group (left). If the group code has expired, add the maintainer (right) at **TZ857886159**.

  

Hit a bug? The code is open — send the error and the [issue-fix prompt](docs/guide/codex-issue-fix-prompt-en.md) to Claude Code or Codex, and it can often patch it for you. Anything everyone runs into, tell us and it goes into the mainline. ## For Teams **Custom builds**, **Integrations**, **AGPL-compliant deployment**, and **Ongoing iteration** for teams that want Nomi inside a real production workflow. [Discuss a project](https://github.com/aqm857886159/Nomi/issues/new?template=business_inquiry.yml) — the form is public, so share only a non-confidential summary and never post credentials, private contact details, budget details, or NDA-protected information. ## Developers Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm. ```bash git clone https://github.com/aqm857886159/Nomi.git cd Nomi corepack enable pnpm install pnpm dev ``` ```text electron/ Electron main process, local runtime, storage, and model calls src/ React + Vite + Tailwind workbench skills/ Skill Pack v2; see docs/skill-pack-format.md ``` Useful checks: `pnpm run test` · `pnpm run typecheck` · `pnpm run gates` Research tooling (searching what creators say on Douyin / Xiaohongshu / Bilibili / X) reads its key only from the `TIKHUB_API_KEY` environment variable — see [`docs/research/tikhub-api-notes.md`](docs/research/tikhub-api-notes.md). ## Contributing Bug reports, feature proposals, documentation, and code contributions are welcome. Contributors do not need to sign a CLA; contributions are ac

details.readme:
coding.sh records what your AI agents do: every prompt, model call, tool call, file change and what it cost.
You read each run in a local viewer and turn the ones that went wrong into evals.
Your sessions stay on your machine.

Docs · Quickstart · Supported agents · What you get · Changelog · Discussions · Report a bug

```sh npx coding.sh # try it: finds your agents, asks once, imports past sessions curl -fsSL https://coding.sh/install | sh # or install it: same setup, then opens the viewer ``` On Windows, run `npx -p coding.sh codingsh` where this page says `npx coding.sh`, and the script in Git Bash. In PowerShell and cmd, type `codingsh` for an installed `coding.sh` ([Windows](docs/guides/install.md#windows)).


A first run of npx coding.sh 0.1.6 in a fresh home.

Run `npx coding.sh` again to open the viewer on your sessions. **What it costs:** nothing. MIT licensed, runs on your machine, no account.


One Claude Code session in the local viewer (coding.sh ui), with the diff it made and the tests it ran.

Each session goes into a SQLite index on your machine, with its latency and tokens. You browse it in a local viewer, query it from the CLI or from your agents over MCP, turn failures into evals, and compare changes with paired statistics. No session data leaves your machine unless you add a remote sink. No runtime dependencies. Node 22.16 or newer. ## Quickstart 1. Run `npx coding.sh`, or the install command above. It runs `coding.sh init`: it finds your agents, shows one plan and asks once. 2. Start a new agent session. Agents read their hooks when a session starts, so one that was already open may not be recorded. 3. Run `coding.sh` to open the viewer. New sessions show up on their own, with no ingest step, and your agents can read them over MCP. `init` points each agent's hooks at coding.sh, registers the MCP server where the agent supports it, and backs up every config file it edits. It also imports the sessions your agents already keep on this machine, so the viewer opens on your own history. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `coding.sh init --dry-run` | Prints the plan without writing anything. `--diff` adds the edits. | | `coding.sh init --no-import` | Sets up capture and skips the past-session import. | | `coding.sh ingest --backfill` | Imports past sessions again, for example after adding an agent. | | `coding.sh uninstall` | Removes the hooks and MCP entries again. |
npm install, the npx cache and other ways to install
You can also install with npm: `npm install -g coding.sh`. If you only ran `npx coding.sh`, the hooks keep recording, but the MCP server runs the copy in the npx cache, so install it before you clear that cache. Installing from source, updates and uninstall: [docs/guides/install.md](docs/guides/install.md).
## What you get | Area | What it does | Start with | |---|---|---| | **Record** | Captures each session, including subagents, from hooks and transcripts. Wraps any other agent. Takes OpenTelemetry from frameworks and apps. | `coding.sh init`, `coding.sh run -- `, `coding.sh collector` | | **Measure** | Turns, tool calls, model calls, tokens, latency and outcome for every session. Flags sessions that edited code and never ran a check. | `coding.sh sessions`, `coding.sh usage`, `coding.sh improve` | | **Evaluate** | Turns a failed session into a replayable eval. Runs experiments with code graders or calibrated LLM judges. A/B tests prompts, harness files and models with paired statistics. | `coding.sh eval new`, `coding.sh exp compare` | | **Benchmark** | Draws new cases every day, runs every contender on the same frozen set, and writes a static report. | `coding.sh bench` | | **Production** | One server for ingest, the viewer and the API, backed by SQLite, Postgres or ClickHouse. SDKs for API apps. | `coding.sh serve` |

### Read your sessions ```sh coding.sh sessions # recent sessions coding.sh show latest # timeline with turns, tools, subagents and latency coding.sh search "rate limit" # full-text search over prompts, replies and tool calls coding.sh usage --by model # tokens, turns and cache hits coding.sh stats --by agent # sessions, failures, cost and latency per agent, with a daily trend coding.sh diff-calls latest#-1 # what changed since the previous model call, and why the cache missed coding.sh ui # the local viewer ``` Every command takes `--json`. `coding.sh mcp` gives your agents the same data as MCP tools. More in [docs/guides/explore.md](docs/guides/explore.md).
Record: wrappers, OpenTelemetry and the model API proxy
- `coding.sh run -- ` wraps any other agent and snapshots the repo before and after. - `coding.sh collector` takes OpenTelemetry from agent frameworks and apps. - `coding.sh init --proxy` routes Claude Code and Codex through a local API proxy that logs each model call's system prompt, tools, messages and cache use. More in [docs/how-to/capture-with-proxy.md](docs/how-to/capture-with-proxy.md).
Evaluate: evals, experiments and paired statistics
Turn a failed session into a replayable eval with `coding.sh eval new`, and check that its verifier is fair with `coding.sh eval validate`. Run experiments over versioned datasets with code graders or calibrated LLM judges. `coding.sh exp compare` and `coding.sh compare` A/B prompts, harness files and models with paired statistics. `coding.sh exp replay` resends one logged model call with another model or system prompt. Tool evals and multi-agent workflow runs are covered too. More in [docs/guides/evals.md](docs/guides/evals.md).
Benchmark: daily cases and head-to-head reports
`coding.sh bench` draws new cases every day from a script, your failed sessions, GitHub issues or a sitemap. Every contender gets the same frozen set in random order, and `bench report` writes a static page with the trend, today's head to head and where each one fails. More in [docs/guides/benchmarks.md](docs/guides/benchmarks.md).
Production: server, SDKs and LLM gateways
`coding.sh serve` runs ingest, the viewer and the API on one port, backed by SQLite, Postgres or ClickHouse. Your API apps send traces with the TypeScript SDK (`@codingdotsh/sdk`), the Python SDK (`coding-sh`) or plain OpenTelemetry. `coding.sh gateway` links calls made through LLM gateways (Vercel AI Gateway, OpenRouter, LiteLLM, Cloudflare, Portkey, Helicone) to their billed cost. The TypeScript SDK and the store plugins are on npm, and the Python SDK is on PyPI. Start with [docs/production/README.md](docs/production/README.md).
## Supported agents


Every agent, one record: the diagram from the coding.sh front page.

| Agent | How it records | Status | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | hooks, transcript, subagents | Verified on real sessions | | Codex CLI | hooks, rollout files, subagents | Verified on real sessions | | Antigravity CLI (formerly Gemini CLI) | hooks, transcript

# Motionboard

Make launch videos and motion graphics with Claude Code or Codex: a free HyperFrames skill with 48 shot recipes (match cut, logo reveal, kinetic typography, liquid glass effect, typing animation and more), each rebuilt in code from Apple, Linear, Figma and other launch films.

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Claude Code skill](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude%20Code-skill-d97757)](#install)
[![Codex skill](https://img.shields.io/badge/Codex-skill-111111)](#install)

[motionboard.app](https://motionboard.app) · [All recipes](https://motionboard.app/#recipes)

[![The Motionboard launch film, built from six recipes](assets/readme/film.gif)](https://motionboard.app)

Ask your agent to "make a launch video for my product", "add a match cut between these two screens" or "animate our logo reveal", and it builds the shot in code and renders an MP4 (or ports the motion to your website). Motionboard breaks real launch films down into 48 shots. Each shot is recreated in code as a ~10 second [HyperFrames](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes) film (HTML and GSAP rendered to video), and the website shows every original next to its recreation. The skill gives your agent all 48 recipes, so it can make one shot or plan and build a whole launch film for your product.

[![Motionboard launch film, made with the Motionboard skill](https://media.motionboard.app/launch-motionboard-motionboard.jpg)](https://media.motionboard.app/launch-motionboard-motionboard.mp4)

The same three products, with the films from HyperFrames and brag next to ours: [launch video examples](https://motionboard.app/guides/launch-video-examples/).

Requirements: Node 22+, HyperFrames (`npx hyperframes`), ffmpeg.

## Install

```sh
npx skills add krisyangdev/motionboard
```

Or hand the link to your agent:

> Install this skill: https://github.com/krisyangdev/motionboard

Agents installing for a user: run `npx skills add krisyangdev/motionboard -g -y` (global, no prompts). If the skill is not available in the current session yet, read `SKILL.md` at the path the command prints (usually `~/.agents/skills/motionboard/`) and follow it.

In Claude Code, add it as a plugin:

```sh
/plugin marketplace add krisyangdev/motionboard
/plugin install motionboard@motionboard
```

Manual install for Claude Code and Codex:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/krisyangdev/motionboard.git ~/motionboard
ln -s ~/motionboard/skills/motionboard ~/.claude/skills/motionboard
ln -s ~/motionboard/skills/motionboard ~/.codex/skills/motionboard
```

## Use

| Say | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Make a launch film for my product with Motionboard. | The agent reads your product, proposes a 4 to 6 shot storyboard with preview links, waits for your OK, builds each shot and joins them into one MP4. |
| Make a launch film for https://your-product.com with Motionboard. | One command, no questions: the agent captures the page, writes a brief, picks five recipes, builds and renders each one, and joins them into a 22 to 32 second MP4. |
| Use the match-cut recipe to go from my logo to the app. | The agent builds that one shot with your brand and UI, renders it, and checks it against the preview. |
| Make the Tilted UI with Depth of Field shot for this landing page. | The agent ports the recipe's GSAP timeline into your site as a hero animation. |

Each recipe page on [motionboard.app](https://motionboard.app) has a copy button that gives your agent one line: install this skill, then make that shot.
